summary:
MACSym is a medical monitoring and interpretation system designed to support astronauts during space missions. It connects to wearable sensors and medical equipment to collect and analyze health data in real time, enabling rapid responses to emergencies without waiting for communication with Earth.
The system interprets vital signs and medical test results using predefined reference values and presents information in simple, understandable language. Its interactive human body visualization highlights potentially problematic organs and areas, helping astronauts and medical personnel identify health concerns.
MACSym also includes personalized astronaut profiles, medical history tracking, test result monitoring, and graphs showing changes in health indicators over time. It allows astronauts to plan physical activities, while medical professionals can create and adjust personalized training programs based on individual health conditions.
A friendly virtual assistant, Space Pony, explains medical information and provides predefined recommendations based on analyzed data. Access levels ensure full system functionality for onboard medical personnel and Earth-based administrators.
MACSym aims to improve astronaut safety, accelerate medical decision-making, support physical well-being, and make complex medical information accessible during missions far from Earth.
details:
MACSym (Medical Autonomical Calculation System) is a Windows desktop application designed to monitor, interpret, and support astronauts' health during space missions. It combines medical data analysis, health visualization, personalized physical training, and emotional support in one platform.

The application provides an interactive visualization of the human body, highlighting potentially problematic organs and body areas based on the internal interpretation of medical examination results. Astronauts can personalize their virtual avatars, monitor their medical history, track changes in health indicators, and receive regular notifications about their health and planned physical activities. MACSym also includes a training management system that allows astronauts to organize their workouts, while medical professionals can develop personalized exercise programs based on individual health conditions. Areas of the body requiring additional physical training are visually highlighted to help users understand where they should focus their efforts.

An important feature of the application is its friendly virtual assistant, Space Pony, which explains medical examination results in simple, accessible language and provides predefined recommendations based on the available medical data. MACSym does not rely on AI agents or cloud-based services for medical interpretation. Instead, all calculations and interpretations are performed locally using predefined medical reference values and rules stored within the application. This approach allows the system to function independently of internet access and continuous communication with Earth.

The current prototype requires medical information to be entered manually. However, future development aims to integrate wearable sensors attached to astronauts' bodies and medical laboratory equipment, enabling automated data collection and real-time health monitoring.

The main benefit of MACSym is the ability to provide astronauts with immediate access to medical information and explanations without waiting for data transmission to Earth and feedback from ground-based specialists. It can help reduce delays in identifying potential health problems, support preventive healthcare, encourage regular physical activity, and improve astronauts' independence during long-duration missions. Space Pony also adds a friendly and motivating element, making medical information less intimidating and encouraging astronauts to take an active role in maintaining their well-being.

The intended impact of MACSym is to contribute to safer and more sustainable human space exploration by providing astronauts with an accessible onboard medical support system. Our team considered astronaut safety, ease of use, personalization, limited connectivity in space, and the psychological challenges of long-duration missions. We wanted to create not just another medical monitoring application, but a digital companion that supports astronauts' physical health, helps them understand their bodies, and makes taking care of themselves a more comfortable and engaging experience.

The project was developed using Python as the primary programming language and Flet, a Python framework based on Flutter, to create the graphical user interface for Windows.
